Description

Eicosanoids made in the joint act on nociceptors and in the spinal cord. Several lipoxygenase products, 12(S)- and 15(S)-HpETE, 5(S)- and 15(S)-HETE and LTB4, open the capsaicin receptor TRPV1 of sensory neurons (Hwang 2000), and hepoxilin A3 opens TRPV1 and TRPA1 (Gregus 2012). The cyclopentenone prostaglandins 15d-PGJ2 and PGA2 cause pain through TRPA1 (Materazzi 2008), as does 5,6-EET at the central terminals of sensory neurons (Sisignano 2012). The cysteinyl leukotriene receptor CysLT2 is expressed by TRPV1 and P2X3 positive sensory neurons, and LTC4 strengthens the pain evoked through P2X3 (Okubo 2010). In the spinal cord PGD2 inhibits allodynia through DP receptors (Minami 1997) and causes it through DP2 on spinal neurons (Kanda 2013). Lipoxin A4 acts on its receptor on spinal astrocytes and attenuates inflammatory pain (Svensson 2007).

Colour

Red raises pain, blue relieves it, and olive acts both ways. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block.

The mediators that open TRPV1 and TRPA1, and LTC4 with CysLT2, are red. DP1, lipoxin A4 and its receptor are blue, DP2 is red. PGD2 and 15d-PGJ2 are olive, as they act both ways: 15d-PGJ2 also relieves joint pain (Pena-dos-Santos 2009).
